answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each node to a Wesolowski VDF requiring a prescribed sequence of modular squarings, with every result feeding the next and a succinct proof checking the completed chain. An attacker may launch clone instances on GPUs, but cannot parallelize the dependencies within any instance, so each clone still incurs the same irreducible wall-clock delay and hardware cost. A juniper cipher stored in a vault may authenticate context, but cannot bypass this sequential bottleneck.
